message.content:
**Common proteins that reside in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical proteins | Function | |----------|------------------|----------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** – pumps Na⁺ out and K⁺ in
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** – passive glucose transport
• **Aquaporin‑4** – water channel
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., β₂‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** – e.g., epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)
• **Ion channels** – e.g., voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv), calcium channel (Cav)
• **Integrins** – cell‑matrix adhesion (α₁β₁, α₄β₇, etc.)
• **Cadherins** – cell‑cell adhesion (E‑cadherin, N‑cadherin)
• **Connexins** – gap junction channels (Cx43, Cx32)
• **Claudins** – tight‑junction strands (Claudin‑1, Claudin‑4) | Transport, signaling, adhesion, cell communication | | **Peripheral (surface‑associated) proteins** | • **Annexins** – bind phospholipids in a Ca²⁺‑dependent manner
• **Spectrin** – cytoskeletal support
• **Band‑3 protein** – anion exchanger in red‑blood‑cell membranes
• **Glycophorins** – sialylated glycoproteins on erythrocytes
• **MHC class I & II molecules** – antigen presentation (though they are integral, they are often listed as peripheral in functional contexts) | Structural support, signaling, immune recognition | These proteins are among the most frequently cited examples when discussing the composition of the plasma membrane. They illustrate the diverse roles—transport, signaling, adhesion, and structural integrity—that membrane proteins play in cellular physiology.
